run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T12:48:36Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for service_name=frontend-proxy (namespace otel-demo, severity warning, firing since 2026-11-16T12:48:36Z, annotation current 0.01111111111111111) is backed by real error spans: frontend-proxy emits STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on both of its operations, the server span 'ingress' (HTTP 503 returned to callers such as load-generator) and the client span 'router frontend egress'. In every sampled failing trace the client egress span ends with error=true and http.status_code=0, and the complete trace contains no frontend span, so the request failed on the frontend-proxy -> frontend hop without the frontend application returning an HTTP response. The error volume is small in absolute terms (34.44 error spans versus 56,621.73 UNSET spans over the hour ending 13:08:45Z) and is dominated by a single burst: in the 1-minute bucket at 12:43:00Z frontend-proxy's error increase is 26 (all other buckets 0-6) and frontend's is 18. In that same minute product-catalog's span increase collapses to 122 from 1288-1622 in adjacent minutes, immediately after the product-catalog Deployment was restarted (template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T12:41:11Z, old pod deleted 12:41:15Z, replacement pod created 12:41:11Z with its container started 12:41:14Z) and that Deployment defines no readiness probe. That is the best-supported explanation for the dominant burst, stated as a hypothesis. A residual low-rate 503 pattern (about 1-2 proxy errors per minute, seen before and after the restart, e.g. trace b303e7616d6cc9296844951cbe4749d5 at 12:29Z) is not explained by the restart and remains unresolved; candidates are intermittent connection failure on the same-node frontend-proxy -> frontend hop or frontend accept/queue saturation under sustained CPU throttling (CFS throttle ratio 0.26-0.33 on pod frontend), but no available telemetry confirms either. The alerting entity itself was not crashed: frontend-proxy and frontend pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, all 21 otel-demo deployments are 1/1 available, the frontend Service has its single correct endpoint, all five nodes are Ready, and frontend served 200s normally with steady 12,777-13,426 spans per 5 min. The alert's exact expression and threshold are unknown because no Prometheus rules are exposed, and the annotated 0.0111 could not be reproduced from the available span metrics.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's only span operations in Jaeger are 'ingress' (span_kind server) and 'router frontend egress' (span_kind client).

frontend-proxy produced STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on both operations during the window: span_name='ingress' span_kind=SPAN_KIND_SERVER errors of about 1.1-10 per 5 min and span_name='router frontend egress' span_kind=SPAN_KIND_CLIENT errors of about 6.7-7.0 per 5 min at the peak, against roughly 2,930-3,210 UNSET spans per 5 min per operation.

Whole-window increase ending 2026-11-16T13:08:45Z for service_name=frontend-proxy: 34.435897435897445 ERROR spans versus 56621.73076923078 UNSET spans, about 0.06% of frontend-proxy spans carried an error status in that hour.

At minute resolution frontend-proxy's ERROR-span increase jumps to 26 in the bucket at 2026-11-16T12:43:00Z while all other 1-minute buckets are 0-6, and frontend's ERROR-span increase jumps to 18 in that same single bucket with all other buckets 0.
In the same 12:43:00Z bucket product-catalog's span increase falls to 122 from 1288 and 1460-1622 in the adjacent minutes; product-catalog has only a STATUS_CODE_UNSET series and no ERROR series.

The product-catalog Deployment was restarted: template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T12:41:11Z, its events show ScalingReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9 from 0 to 1 with SuccessfulCreate at 12:41:11Z and SuccessfulDelete of pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp at 12:41:15Z, and replacement pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 was created 12:41:11Z with its container started 12:41:14Z.
The product-catalog container has no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe, with resource limits cpu 15m and memory 30Mi and env GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB.

Every sampled failing trace has the same shape: load-generator GET (error=true, http.status_code 503) -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' server span (error=true, http.status_code 503, otel.status_code ERROR) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' client span (error=true, http.status_code 0); the complete trace b303e7616d6cc9296844951cbe4749d5 contains exactly these four spans and no frontend span.

frontend's error spans in the 12:43:00Z bucket are distributed over span_name GET span_kind SERVER (5.55), POST SERVER (1.11), POST /api/checkout SERVER (1.11), 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' INTERNAL (1.11) and tcp.connect INTERNAL (1.11), and the ERROR series for grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and GET /api/products/{productId} first appear with their first sample at 12:43:36Z.

Across all otel-demo services only ad, frontend, frontend-proxy and recommendation had nonzero ERROR-span increases in the window; accounting, fraud-detection and payment stayed at 0 and product-catalog shows no ERROR series at all.

At query time all 21 otel-demo pods were Running and Ready with restartCount 0, all 21 otel-demo deployments had desired=1, available=1, ready=1, and all five nodes were Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False.

frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56 were created at 2026-11-16T12:08:09Z and 12:08:10Z by ReplicaSets frontend-675fd7b5c5 and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985 owned by Deployments frontend and frontend-proxy; every other otel-demo pod except product-catalog was also created 12:08:09-12:08:12Z, and the product-catalog pod was created 12:41:11Z.

The frontend Service (selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend, port 8080) has exactly one endpoint 100.96.3.42:8080 belonging to pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw, and the frontend-proxy Service endpoint 100.96.3.19:8080 belongs to pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56.

frontend was serving successfully during the window: its sampled spans at 12:37Z (GET, POST, GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/data and grpc.oteldemo.* client calls) all carry http.status_code 200 or rpc.grpc.status_code 0, and its span volume stays at 12,777-13,426 per 5 min through 12:58Z.

Sustained CFS throttling was present on both pods: throttled-period ratio 0.26-0.33 for pod frontend and 0.027-0.054 for pod frontend-proxy across 12:23-13:03Z, with CPU usage about 0.047 cores for frontend (limit 100m) and about 0.0115 cores for frontend-proxy (limit 30m).
Memory readings: frontend RSS 112-123 MB against a 200Mi limit (working set including cache 239-262 MB) and frontend-proxy RSS about 19 MB against a 50Mi limit (working set about 41 MB).

product-catalog's retrieved log lines show normal serving text 'Product Found' and periodic 'Reloading Product Catalog...' / 'Loaded 10 products' entries, with no error-level text in the lines returned.

The alerting service's own pod was not crashing or restarting: frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56 is ready with restartCount 0, empty lastState and creation time 12:08:10Z, and Deployment frontend-proxy has 1/1 available replicas.

product-catalog itself shows no error status and normal throughput outside the single 12:42-12:43Z minute (1288-1622 spans per minute at 12:41 and 12:44-12:55), so a sustained product-catalog outage is not supported by its own signals.
Rejected: the frontend container was OOMKilled or restarted. frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw has restartCount 0, empty lastState, RSS 112-123 MB against a 200Mi memory limit, and steady span throughput.

Rejected: the frontend Service or its endpoints were misconfigured. The Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend on port 8080 has a single endpoint 100.96.3.42:8080 that is the running frontend pod, and frontend-proxy resolves to its own running pod endpoint.

The dominant error burst is explained by the product-catalog rollout restart at 2026-11-16T12:41:11Z: the replacement pod had no readiness gate and served only 122 spans in the 12:42-12:43 minute versus 1288-1622 normally; in that same minute frontend emitted 18 error spans including the first ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and GET /api/products/{productId} ERROR samples, and frontend-proxy emitted its largest error count of 26. Requests frontend could not complete upstream ended at the proxy as 503 responses with no upstream HTTP status.

The residual low-rate 503 pattern (about 1-2 proxy errors per minute outside 12:41-12:44Z, e.g. trace b303e7616d6cc9296844951cbe4749d5 at 12:29Z with a 954 ms egress span ending error=true and http.status_code 0 and no frontend span) is not explained by the product-catalog restart. Candidate causes that remain unverified are intermittent connection failure on the same-node frontend-proxy -> frontend hop (both pods on node i-0d38f3ed4102a442f) or frontend accept/queue saturation under sustained 0.26-0.33 CFS throttling; no packet-loss, backlog or connection-error telemetry is available to discriminate them.

Add readinessProbes to the otel-demo workloads that lack them, starting with product-catalog, so Service traffic reaches a pod only once the process can serve, then re-check whether rollout minutes still coincide with frontend and frontend-proxy error bursts.

Review the tight resource settings behind the observed throttling: product-catalog (cpu 15m, memory 30Mi, GOMEMLIMIT 16MiB) and frontend (cpu 100m, observed about 0.047 cores used with 0.26-0.33 of CFS periods throttled), and measure p99 latency before and after any change.

To close the unresolved hop, load the RequestErrorRate rule definition into the queried Prometheus and pull frontend-proxy Envoy access-log response flags (UH/UF/UT) plus packet-loss and retransmit counters for node i-0d38f3ed4102a442f for the error minutes.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not exposed by the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and unfiltered both returned no_data, so the rule expression, threshold, window and the annotated value 0.0111 could not be verified; the span-derived error ratios observed (34.44 errors versus 56,621.73 UNSET spans over the hour ending 13:08:45Z) do not reproduce 1.11%.

No kube-state-metrics series are present in the queryable Prometheus (get_metric_names for {__name__=~"kube_.*"} and a kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total query both returned no_data), so pod readiness and restart history during the incident window is unknown; only live Kubernetes object state was available.

Jaeger returned no_data for the 12:41-12:45Z burst interval (traces_search_by_tags service=frontend-proxy, tag http.status_code=503, 12:41-12:45:30Z) and traced spans begin at 12:18:30Z, so the burst traces themselves could not be inspected and events before 12:18Z remain unknown.

The frontend container returned no log lines for the queried windows (12:18-13:05Z with an error filter and 12:40-12:45Z unfiltered, both no_data), so frontend application-side errors could be neither confirmed nor excluded.

frontend-proxy logs earlier than about 12:49:50Z were not readable because the 4 MiB read limit was reached while reading from 12:30Z (view truncated at read_through 12:50:07Z), and a targeted 12:49:30-12:51:30Z search for lines containing ' 503 ' returned no_data, so Envoy response flags for the failing minutes are unknown.
No span metrics exist before 12:18:36Z, so whether the 503s predate the namespace-wide pod recreation at 12:08:09-12:08:12Z or began with it is unknown.
No network-level telemetry (packet loss, retransmits, accept-queue or backlog, conntrack) is available, so the connectivity or saturation hypothesis for the residual low-rate 503s cannot be tested.

The NetworkPolicy query for otel-demo returned no_data and the ConfigMap query returned only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products, so no Envoy/frontend-proxy configuration is available for review and whether any traffic policy existed or changed during the window is unknown.
next_steps: A human with rule access should supply the RequestErrorRate recording/alerting rule definition and its evaluation window so the annotated 0.0111 can be reconciled with the span-derived error ratio.

Inspect the otel-demo frontend-proxy Envoy admin/access logs (response flags UH/UF/UT) and frontend application logs for 12:41-12:44Z and for the steady-state 503 minutes, which were not readable within the read limits of this Run.
Add readiness probes to product-catalog and any other workload missing them, then verify whether later product-catalog rollouts still coincide with frontend-proxy 503 bursts.

Collect CFS throttling and container log evidence for frontend and frontend-proxy over a longer window, and consider raising the 100m CPU limit on the frontend and the 30m limit on frontend-proxy if throttling correlates with the residual 503 rate.

Enable and query network-level metrics (retransmits, packet loss, socket backlog) for node i-0d38f3ed4102a442f, where frontend-proxy and frontend run, to test the intermittent-connection hypothesis for the low-rate 503s.

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
